Alex — thanks and congrats again. Attached is a concise MAP draft that embeds the post-signature implementation plan and includes the canary, migration and training schedules (2025-06-05_Redwood_MAP_v1.pdf). High-level summary below: 

Rollout phases:
- Phase 0 (pre-provisioning, 6/9–6/13): infra & IAM, baseline tests, model pinning.
- Phase 1 (canary, 6/16–6/18): 5% traffic, weekend window, automated KPIs monitor + manual checkpoint.
- Phase 2 (staged migration, 6/19–6/27): 25% -> 50% -> 100% across regional pools with surge capacity.
- Phase 3 (training & knowledge transfer, 6/23–6/30): ops runbooks, runbook drills, one-week shadowed support.

Canary specifics:
- Scope: API endpoints only (generation + embeddings), subset of 3 internal teams then external beta users.
- Gate metrics: error rate <0.5% sustained over 2 hours; 95th latency <550ms; no regression on 10 curated eval prompts.
- Rollback: immediate rollback to previous model variant + traffic re-routed to fallback pool if gate breached.

Training plan (ops):
- 3 live sessions (2 hours each) + 4 office-hours drop-ins. Materials: runbooks, monitoring dashboard walkthrough, incident-playbook.
- Suggested training dates: 6/23, 6/25, 6/27 (all 10:00–12:00 PT).

Acceptance & procurement milestone to add (per your MAT):
- Procurement confirms license terms and issues purchase order by 6/12.
- Final invoice sent on 6/13; go/no-go meeting on 6/15 before canary.

I've kept the MAP focused on executional checkpoints so your procurement and IT teams can map tasks to their trackers. Please review and let us know where to sync with Security for the SOC-related evidence.

Attachments: 2025-06-05_Redwood_MAP_v1.pdf

Thanks,

Adding ops notes from my side — a few operational tweaks to reduce blast radius: 

1) Canary day/time: recommend starting the canary on Tuesday 6/17 at 0200–0800 PT (lower traffic), not weekend — makes on-call rotation simpler and we can leverage 6/16 for a dry run.
2) Canary by user-segmentation: start with internal power users (3 teams), then a controlled cohort of 50 external dev keys, then open.
3) Migration cadence: ensure DB migration is read-only during 25% -> 50% increment step to avoid drift; schedule schema freezes if required.
4) Observability: we need to pre-open a short-lived support channel in Slack + Pager duty schedule for the full phased window.

I attached a lightweight training roster suggestion (training_roster_week1.csv). Also, we should add a regression eval run immediately prior to canary (we'll do the 10 eval prompts + 3 customer-specific prompts).
